data.title: Vietnam passes law to speed up land expropriation for priority projects
data.description:
Key points:
  • Law aims to ease delays to infrastructure, industrial projects
  • Under new law expropriation decisions could be made before compensation determined

Vietnam's parliament approved a law on Saturday to speed up the expropriation of land in the case of some special projects, a move that could boost infrastructure development while reducing the leverage of farmers in fighting such seizures.

The legislation aims to ease delays to infrastructure and industrial projects in Vietnam, many of which have been held back by complaints from residents and farmers that compensation for expropriated land was below market value.

Under the revised land law, authorities may issue land-expropriation decisions before compensation plans are approved, provided no resettlement is required and the plans have been publicly disclosed.

The provision applies to nationally important projects, urgent public-investment projects, cases where more than 75% of affected land users agree to the expropriation.

"From a technical standpoint, the provision appears designed to facilitate timely implementation of priority projects while retaining procedural safeguards," said Chris Luong, a partner at CNC Counsel, a law firm specialising in construction, infrastructure and real estate.

Among the 479 National Assembly deputies, five opposed the revised land law and eight did not cast a vote. The law will be implemented from July 1, 2027.

The revised law introduces additional safeguards for people whose land is expropriated, including stronger resettlement protections, livelihood support for up to three years and expanded vocational training, Minister of Agriculture and Environment Trinh Viet Hung told parliament on Saturday.

Previously, compensation plans generally had to be approved before the land could be expropriated.

The change could be particularly relevant for agricultural land, where expropriation is less likely to require households to relocate, rather than in cases involving residential property, Luong said.

Application of the law would, however, still depend on the project type and the prescribed consent thresholds, he said.

Land disputes have long been a sensitive issue in Vietnam, where negotiations over compensation often drag on for years and ⁠occasionally ​trigger protests in the tightly controlled ​country.

In Hanoi, some residents living along the Red River earlier this year hung banners and marched through their neighbourhood urging authorities to reconsider a proposed $28 billion redevelopment plan that could affect about 280,000 people.

Another high-profile case involves a Trump Organization-backed golf project in northern Hung Yen province that includes farmland acquired from local residents.

Lawmakers said the revised law would also introduce clearer criteria for land acquisitions and reform the way land is valued with more transparent, data-driven pricing methods.

Lawmakers also passed a data security law expanding state oversight of sensitive data and cross-border data flows, and approved changes to the criminal code that remove the death penalty for six offences, including drug trafficking and child rape.

data.title: LEPAS L8 PHEV Makes Its Gulf Debut, Bringing Elegant Mobility to the Middle East
data.description:
DUBAI, United Arab Emirates and WUHU, China, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- LEPAS, Chery Auto’s Premium NEV brand, officially entered the Gulf market with a regional brand launch in Dubai. Its first model in the region, the LEPAS L8, is now on sale in the UAE, starting at AED 99,999, with launches in Kuwait, Qatar and other markets to follow.

As the Gulf accelerates its transition to new energy mobility, policy support and interest in electrified vehicles continue to grow. Customers seek vehicles that combine distinctive design with the ability to handle diverse road and climate conditions. The LEPAS L8 PHEV meets these expectations as an Elegant All-round Premium SUV, bringing together refined design, confident driving and intelligent technology.

The first 100 customers will receive exclusive benefits, including insurance, maintenance and complimentary roadside assistance. LEPAS also offers a 7-year/200,000-km vehicle warranty and an 8-year/160,000-km warranty for the electric powertrain system, providing added peace of mind.

Elegant Design: Where Natural Energy Meets Spacious Comfort

Created for customers who appreciate bold design and refined details, the LEPAS L8 PHEV embodies Leopard Aesthetics, inspired by the agility and strength of the leopard. Flowing body lines and the distinctive Leaping Leopard Beltline create a dynamic sense of movement, while the Pioneering Leopard Avant-Garde Front Fascia and Leopard-Eye LED Headlights give the SUV a commanding yet expressive presence.

With a 2,800-mm wheelbase and 66.5% space utilization, the LEPAS L8 PHEV offers a spacious five-seat layout. Its wraparound cabin creates a welcoming atmosphere, complemented by Cloud Comfort Lounge Seats and excellent NVH performance for a quiet, comfortable ride. A 507L cargo capacity, 47 Ingenious Storage Spaces and versatile seating configurations make room for passengers and everyday essentials alike, turning the cabin into a comfortable living space on the move.

Elegant Driving: Smart Assistance Makes Journeys Easier

Built on the intelligent LEX Platform, the LEPAS L8 PHEV features APA and RPA Parking Assistance to simplify parking in busy urban environments, from maneuvering in tight spaces to parking in designated spaces in multi-level garages. Its 16 ADAS features also assist with following distance, lane keeping and hazard detection, making daily commutes and intercity journeys easier.

For greater awareness in busy streets and at turns with limited visibility, the LEPAS L8 PHEV features 540° Panoramic View. A cage-style body structure, six airbags and a battery pack with IP68 and IPX9K protection ratings provide additional layers of safety and reassurance.

Local Adaptation: Balancing Driving Efficiency with Everyday Needs

Powered by LEPAS Super Hybrid, the L8 PHEV balances energy efficiency with extended range for daily commutes and longer journeys. Under the NEDC test cycle, it delivers a combined range of up to 1,300 km and an all-electric range of more than 100 km, with charging from 30% to 80% taking just 20 minutes. Whether commuting or travelling beyond the city, customers can enjoy greater flexibility on the road.

The L8 PHEV is also adapted to the region’s hot climate. Its upgraded air-conditioning system, combined with UV-Blocking and Heat-Insulating Glass, helps keep the cabin cool under intense sunlight. Meanwhile, the AQS Air Quality Monitoring System monitors cabin air quality, ensuring a fresh and comfortable interior.

The L8 PHEV marks the beginning of LEPAS’s broader presence in the Middle East. More LEPAS NEV models will follow, expanding choices for local customers. The brand will also continue to co-create with customers across the region, drawing on diverse cultures and perspectives to shape new expressions of elegant living and bring its brand promise, “Drive Your Elegance,” to more people worldwide.

About LEPAS

LEPAS is Chery Auto's Premium NEV brand, dedicated to creating elegant mobility experiences for users worldwide. Committed to becoming the Preferred Brand for Elegant Mobility Life, LEPAS brings together Leopard Aesthetics, Elegant Technology, and Exquisite Space - transforming elegance into a driving experience you can see, feel, and trust. Supported by a growing global dealer network of more than 500 sales and service outlets, LEPAS is expanding its international footprint through localized operations, delivering products and experiences tailored to users across global markets.

About Chery Auto

Founded in 1997, Chery Auto is a global automotive manufacturer specializing in vehicle development, intelligent technologies, and new energy solutions. The company operates in more than 130 countries and regions, supported by a strong international network of research, production, and strategic partnerships. Chery Auto has remained China’s No. 1 passenger vehicle exporter among Chinese brands for 23 consecutive years. Guided by its global philosophy of "In somewhere, For somewhere, Be somewhere," Chery Auto is committed to advancing sustainable mobility through continuous innovation and global collaboration.

data.title: Peter Schiff Says Gold's $2,000 Pullback Could Be A Warning — 'Stocks Will Ultimately Fall Much Further'
data.description:
Key points:
  • Schiff pointed to gold's performance during the 2008 financial crisis, when the precious metal fell roughly 30% before bottoming in October that year.
  • He noted that stocks continued to tumble for months, with the S&P 500 eventually falling nearly 60% from its peak before bottoming in March 2009.
  • Schiff added that gold subsequently staged a massive recovery, rising 166% from its 2008 bottom to its 2011 peak and nearly doubling its previous 2008 high.

Gold's sharp retreat from its record highs may not be a reason for investors to panic, but rather a warning sign of a broader financial crisis ahead, according to economist and longtime gold bull Peter Schiff.

Drawing parallels with the 2008 financial crisis, Schiff argued in posts on X that gold could be repeating a familiar pattern in which the precious metal bottoms before stocks, potentially setting the stage for another major rally as equities continue to slide.

Schiff Sees A 2008 Repeat As Gold Falls Ahead Of Stocks

Schiff pointed to gold's performance during the 2008 financial crisis, when the precious metal fell roughly 30% before bottoming in October that year. He noted that stocks continued to tumble for months, with the S&P 500 eventually falling nearly 60% from its peak before bottoming in March 2009.

The economist added that gold subsequently staged a massive recovery, rising 166% from its 2008 bottom to its 2011 peak and nearly doubling its previous 2008 high, while stocks remained well below their pre-crisis levels.

Schiff believes a similar pattern could be unfolding again, only with a potentially more severe financial crisis ahead.

"Just like in 2008, gold is again falling first, but stocks will ultimately fall much further," Schiff said.

He added that stocks could continue falling even after gold reverses higher, with the precious metal potentially reaching fresh record highs while equities remain significantly below their previous peaks.

Spot gold prices fell 2.41% to $3,538 per ounce on Friday.

Schiff Says Debt And Inflation Could Fuel Gold's Next Rally

Gold has fallen roughly $200 over the past two days and more than $2,000 from its 2026 record high, but Schiff believes the retreat could offer investors an opportunity rather than signal the end of the rally. Gold prices hit a high of $5,595 on Jan. 29, 2026.

He argued that gold's earlier surge was driven by concerns over rising federal debt and inflation, prompting central banks to reduce their exposure to the dollar and turn toward gold.

Schiff believes those forces are likely to intensify rather than fade, potentially setting the stage for another powerful move higher in gold.

"The reason gold hit that record was that rising federal debt & inflation caused central banks to flee the dollar in favor of gold," Schiff said.

"Debt & inflation will soon soar higher than ever," he added, urging investors to take advantage of gold's latest decline.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 1.11%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) rose 1.53%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) surged 0.94%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: Hong Kong Bill Proposes HK$100,000 Fine for Unauthorized Crypto Titles, Two-Year Jail Term for Fake License Claims
data.description:
Hong Kong’s proposed virtual asset legislation would penalize unauthorized use of regulated service-provider titles and false claims of being a license applicant. According to Foresight News, citing Caixin, the 2026 Virtual Asset Service Legislation (Amendment) Bill introduces two offenses to address misleading promotions in the sector.

Anyone who is not licensed or registered but uses titles associated with virtual asset service providers regulated by the Securities and Futures Commission, such as “crypto trader,” “cryptocurrency adviser” or “virtual asset custodian,” could face a HK$100,000 fine upon conviction. Continuing violations would carry an additional HK$2,000 fine for each day they persist.

A person falsely claiming to be a license applicant could, upon conviction on indictment, face a HK$400,000 fine and up to two years in prison. Each day of a continuing offense could bring an additional HK$10,000 fine.

data.title: Dutch court bars Chinese SUV in Europe over resemblance to Land Rover Defender
data.description:
A Dutch district court in The Hague on Friday issued ​an injunction barring European Union sales of a large SUV made by China’s BYD, ‌saying it infringes on the design of Jaguar Land Rover’s popular Defender model.

JLR, ​a unit of India’s Tata Motors, launched the case earlier ⁠this year after BYD announced on its UK website that the seven-seater Ti7 SUV was available for orders with deliveries to customers starting in January 2027.

BYD launched the Fangchengbao Ti7 ‌in China last year.

The Defender is JLR’s most popular model, with global sales of over 100,000 units in 2025.

“In these summary proceedings, ‌the preliminary relief judge rules that the Ti7 infringes the EU design of ‌Jaguar ⁠Land Rover,” the court ruling said. “The characteristic and distinctive elements of the ⁠design are reflected in the BYD Ti7.”

According to automotive media, among the visual similarities between the two vehicles are a boxy, flat-roof silhouette, upright proportions, tailgate styling, squared-off wheel arches and a solid body-colored ​panel behind the rear passenger ‌door.

The injunction will take effect a week after the ruling because BYD “currently has no concrete plans to place the Ti7 on the market in the EU.”

Until the intellectual property case is resolved, the court also banned BYD from producing ‌the vehicle at its new factory in Hungary, which is due to ​start mass-producing cars early next year.

The judge ruled, however, that the court had no jurisdiction over BYD’s affiliate in the United Kingdom.

It ⁠is rare in Europe for major automakers to go to court over design rights infringement. It is also uncommon for such a ruling to come so early ‌in proceedings of a case that is ongoing and likely to last for some time.

“We protect our intellectual property and take legal action when necessary,” JLR said in a statement. “Legal proceedings are ongoing, and we won’t be commenting further at this time.”

Legacy automakers have often complained that Chinese automakers have copied designs, though little has been proven in court. In 2005, for instance, General Motors and Chinese ‌rival Chery settled a case over the Chery QQ that the No. 1 US automaker said was ​a copy of its Chevrolet Spark.

In a statement, BYD said it “strongly disagrees” with the ruling and will appeal it.

“The BYD Ti ⁠7 is the result of BYD’s own independent design work and infringes none of JLR’s ⁠rights,” BYD said. “We will pursue every legal avenue to demonstrate that this decision is incorrect.”

BYD has grown rapidly in Europe since launching sales on ‌the continent in late 2022. According to ACEA data, the Chinese automaker’s sales more than doubled to over 280,000 vehicles in Europe this year through September ​over the same period last year, outselling Ford, Tesla and Nissan.

data.title: SEBI proposes easing disclosure norms for foreign portfolio investors, seeks public comments
data.description:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has proposed to do away with its Additional Disclosure Framework (ADF) for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs), in a move aimed at easing compliance requirements for overseas investors and making Indian capital markets more attractive as an investment destination.

In a consultation paper, the market regulator has proposed removing the existing framework that requires specified categories of FPIs to provide granular details of all entities holding any ownership or economic interest, or exercising control in the fund, on a full look-through basis up to the level of natural persons, without any minimum ownership threshold.

SEBI has also proposed removing the additional disclosure requirements applicable to subscribers of Offshore Derivative Instruments (ODIs) and segregated portfolios maintained by FPIs.

The regulator has sought public comments on the proposal, with December 11, 2026, being the last date for submission.

WHAT IS THE EXISTING ADDITIONAL DISCLOSURE FRAMEWORK?

Under the existing framework, certain FPIs are required to disclose granular details of every entity holding any ownership, economic interest or exercising control in the fund. The disclosure requirement extends through the entire ownership chain up to the level of natural persons, without any threshold.

The framework applies to FPIs meeting either of two criteria:

  • Concentration criteria: FPIs holding more than 50% of their Indian equity assets under management (AUM) in a single Indian corporate group.
  • Size criteria: FPIs which, individually or along with their investor group, hold more than ₹50,000 crore of equity AUM in Indian markets.

The size threshold was originally ₹25,000 crore and was increased to ₹50,000 crore through a circular issued in 2025.

Certain categories of FPIs, including broad-based pooled structures with a widespread investor base and those with government or government-related ownership, are exempt from the additional disclosure requirements, subject to conditions.

WHY IS SEBI PROPOSING TO REMOVE THE FRAMEWORK?

SEBI's primary argument is that India's additional disclosure requirements go significantly beyond the beneficial ownership identification requirements prescribed under existing money-laundering rules and are unique to India.

The regulator has highlighted that several developed and emerging markets that are compliant with Financial Action Task Force (FATF) standards follow a beneficial ownership threshold of 25%. These include the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Luxembourg, Belgium, Portugal, the Netherlands, France, Germany, Singapore, Japan and Hong Kong.

In comparison, India's Prevention of Money Laundering Rules prescribe a controlling ownership interest threshold of 10% or 15%, depending on the legal form of the client.

FATF Recommendation 10 requires financial institutions to undertake client due diligence and identify beneficial owners. While FATF allows individual jurisdictions to prescribe their own ownership thresholds, it recommends that such thresholds should not exceed 25%.

SEBI has noted that India follows a more stringent regime for beneficial ownership identification compared with several other jurisdictions.

The consultation paper argues that disclosure requirements that are not aligned with globally accepted practices could place India at a competitive disadvantage when competing for global capital.

The regulator has also pointed out that foreign capital plays an important role in India's economic expansion by bridging the gap between domestic savings and investment requirements and providing vital foreign exchange to support economic growth.

SEBI HIGHLIGHTS OVER ₹5.61 LAKH CRORE OF FPI OUTFLOWS

An important backdrop to the proposed review is the sustained selling by FPIs in Indian equity markets.

According to the consultation paper, FPIs have withdrawn more than ₹5.61 lakh crore (nearly $62.24 billion), from Indian equity markets between October 2024 and October 2026.

SEBI noted that foreign investors have been net sellers for a sustained period beginning late 2024, with the selling accelerating through 2025 and early 2026.

The regulator has acknowledged that there could be several factors behind the FPI outflows. However, it believes that the relatively onerous beneficial ownership identification and disclosure requirements under the ADF, compared with most FATF-compliant developed and emerging markets, necessitate a review of the existing framework.

SEBI has also highlighted that capital is highly mobile in today's global markets and investors have access to a wide universe of markets and securities. Additional compliance requirements could therefore reduce the attractiveness of Indian capital markets for overseas investors.

WHAT ARE THE PRACTICAL CHALLENGES FACED BY FOREIGN INVESTORS?

The consultation paper lists several operational and compliance challenges arising from the existing disclosure framework.

First, FPIs are required to identify and collect information from a significantly larger number of underlying investors for their Indian investments compared with investments in other jurisdictions.

Second, global funds investing across multiple countries are often forced to set up separate funds for their Indian investments because of the different compliance requirements. This results in additional operational and compliance costs.

Third, pooled investment vehicles such as hedge funds face repeated identification exercises and periodic updates because investor holdings can change frequently due to subscriptions and redemptions.

Fourth, several overseas investors may not be accustomed to providing information beyond what is required in their home jurisdictions. This creates practical difficulties in obtaining the requisite information and documentation.

Finally, tracing ownership through multiple layers in complex FPI structures, including fund-of-funds arrangements and segregated portfolios, to identify natural persons can be both time-consuming and costly.

SEBI has argued that these granular disclosure requirements could discourage foreign investors from investing in India altogether.

CONCENTRATION CRITERIA HAVE BECOME AN ENTRY BARRIER

The regulator has specifically flagged the concentration criteria as a potential entry barrier for overseas investors.

The consultation paper states that many foreign investors consider the granular disclosure requirements an additional compliance burden and may choose to avoid investing in India rather than comply with these requirements.

SEBI has also pointed out that even if an FPI holds a concentrated position in a listed entity, its investment is capped at 10% of the shareholding of that listed entity.

The regulator has therefore questioned the need for the additional disclosure burden arising from the concentration criteria.

PN3 AND THE CHANGE IN BENEFICIAL OWNERSHIP DEFINITION

SEBI has also examined the rationale behind the size criteria, which was introduced to address the possibility of investors misusing the FPI route to circumvent restrictions under Press Note 3 (PN3).

PN3, among other conditions, provided that an entity or citizen of a country sharing a land border with India, or an investment where the beneficial owner was a citizen of such a country, could invest in India only through the government approval route.

The consultation paper notes that the definition of beneficial ownership under PN3 was earlier not clearly defined and was understood to include any direct or indirect ownership. Consequently, even a small stake held by a person from a country sharing a land border with India could fall within the purview of PN3 conditions.

However, through Press Note 02 of 2026, dated March 15, 2026, the government reviewed the FDI policy and modified the investment conditions prescribed under PN3.

The definition of beneficial owner has now been clarified to include only those persons who hold ownership above the thresholds prescribed under the Prevention of Money Laundering Rules.

SEBI has observed that FPIs are already required to provide beneficial ownership details as per the thresholds prescribed under these rules.

Accordingly, the regulator believes that the position under PN3, as clarified through Press Note 02, is now similar to the existing beneficial ownership identification requirements applicable to FPIs.

SEBI has therefore questioned whether the additional requirement under ADF to identify every entity holding any ownership, economic interest or control in an FPI that breaches the size criteria is still necessary.

WHAT EXACTLY HAS SEBI PROPOSED?

Taking into account the compliance challenges faced by foreign investors and the changes in the government's FDI policy, SEBI has proposed the following:

- Complete removal of the Additional Disclosure Framework applicable to FPIs.

- Removal of ADF provisions applicable to subscribers of Offshore Derivative Instruments.

- Removal of ADF provisions applicable to segregated portfolios maintained by FPIs.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT?

SEBI has invited comments and suggestions from market participants on its proposal to remove the Additional Disclosure Framework for FPIs.

The last date for submitting public comments is December 11, 2026.

The consultation paper specifically seeks responses to one question: whether stakeholders agree with the proposal to remove the Additional Disclosure Framework for FPIs.

data.title: IndusInd Bank terminates former CEO Sumant Kathpalia, seeks recovery of pay since 2020
data.description:
IndusInd Bank said on Friday it has terminated former top boss Sumant ​Kathpalia’s employment with the bank and is seeking ‌to recover pay spanning his entire tenure, ​following a disciplinary inquiry.

Kathpalia resigned ⁠in April 2025 after IndusInd Bank disclosed incorrect accounting on derivative trades that prompted a $230 million hit ‌to its accounts, throwing the private-sector lender into a crisis that hit ‌its shares and drew regulatory scrutiny.

Disciplinary proceedings and termination

The ‌bank ⁠told Kathpalia he would remain in ⁠employment and then initiated disciplinary proceedings against him. In June 2025 he was suspended, pending completion of the ​proceedings.

Based on the ‌findings of an inquiry report this week, the bank’s board decided to terminate Kathpalia’s employment and invoke applicable malus and clawback ‌provisions with effect from the date of ​his initial appointment as CEO in March 2020.

IndusInd did not disclose ⁠details of the inquiry’s findings.

Reuters could not reach Kathpalia for comment.

Bank seeks recovery of salary and bonuses

Reuters had reported ‌in November 2025 that the lender had begun a process to claw back salary and bonuses from Kathpalia and former deputy CEO Arun Khurana, after an internal review flagged misconduct and misreporting.

Indian banking regulations have ‌allowed clawback provisions in employee contracts since 2019 to ​deter misconduct, but such efforts have been rare.

Business recovery and share performance

IndusInd’s loans and deposits returned ⁠to double-digit growth in the second quarter of ⁠the current fiscal year, the first time since the accounting discrepancies emerged. Its shares ‌are up 16% this year after dropping 10% in 2025.

data.title: Bitcoin Falls Below $60K For First Time Since July, Saylor's MSTR Hits 52-Week Low Amid $14B Paper Loss
data.description:
Key points:
  • Strategy's 850,849 BTC are now worth about $50.2 billion, compared to about $64.2 billion paid, which still leaves a paper loss of about $14 billion.
  • Shares of MSTR fell nearly 10% to about $78, a new 52-week low.
  • Strategy bought back STRC for $228.1 million last week, nearly seven times the $33.4 million it invested in Bitcoin.

Bitcoin (BTC) fell below $60,000 Friday for the first time since July, leaving Michael Saylor's Strategy Inc. (MSTR) roughly $14 billion underwater on its holdings.

Bitcoin traded down around $57,799, down about 24% so far in November. In its latest filing, the company holds 850,849 BTC it bought at an average cost of $75,452 per coin. That adds up to about $64.2 billion. With Bitcoin's price at $59,000, Strategy's holding is worth about $50.2 billion.

Bitcoin’s price was down over 5% over the last 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC dropped to the ‘bearish’ zone from the ‘neutral’ zone, accompanied by ‘high’ chatter levels over the past day.

MSTR Shares Hit Fresh Low: Saylor Holds The Line

With Bitcoin's price down, Strategy shares fell nearly 10% Friday to around $78, hitting its 52-week low. The slide is important because Strategy is funding its Bitcoin with its own shares. As the stock price falls, each additional share it sells generates less revenue.

However, Saylor stuck to his long-term case. On X, Saylor wrote, Bitcoin's "supply is invariant to demand, its terminal inflation rate is zero, and its economic half-life is infinite." On Thursday, Saylor said, "Seller exhaustion will come long before Saylor exhaustion."

MSTR's price was up over 2% in overnight trading. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around MSTR remained in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone, accompanied by ‘high’ chatter levels over the past day.

Back Sees Buying Opportunity

Blockstream CEO Adam Back said in an X post that he was buying MSTR shares at current levels. He compared what 1,000 Strategy shares were worth in Bitcoin at two points this year.

On May 28 late, when STRC hit bottom and Bitcoin was trading at $72,500. 1,000 shares were worth 2.09 BTC. He added that the gap represents "1.5x BTC/share upside."

Back said, "With bitcoin discounted, at $59k it makes more sense to push $STRC to par by temporarily pushing interest rate to 13.5% say and then taper it down 0.25%/mo when btc is $100k."

If Strategy could pick up another 50k BTC in the process, he thinks the extra cost would be worth it.

Buybacks Outpace Bitcoin Buys

Recently, a growing share of the company’s funds has been directed toward holding STRC rather than purchasing Bitcoin. STRC is Strategy's variable-rate preferred stock, designed to trade close to its $100 par value.

Strategy said on Monday it purchased 485 BTC for $33.4 million from Nov. 9 to Nov. 15. Over the same week it spent $228.1 million buying back STRC shares. It covered most of both by selling about 2.09 million common shares.

data.title: KAITO: Token unlock releases up to 17.6 million tokens - Nov 2027
data.description:
In November 2027, KAITO is scheduled to unlock up to 17.6 million tokens. That amount equals 7.29% of circulating supply. The tokens are set aside for several groups and uses: the community, the ecosystem, the foundation, investors, liquidity and the team.

Once the tokens are unlocked, recipients can choose to sell some of them. Sales from those allocations would add selling pressure on KAITO.
